record.paper_title: Dense ideals in topological algebras: some results and open problems
record.original_question: Does there exist an F-algebra, or even a B0-algebra, in which every proper ideal is dense?

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Does there exist an F-algebra (or even a B0-algebra) with all (proper) ideals dense ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological algebra is a (complex) associative algebra $A$ equipped with a Hausdorff vector-space topology making the multiplication separately (equivalently, jointly, in the metrizable complete case) continuous. An $F$-algebra is a topological algebra whose underlying topological vector space is a complete metrizable topological vector space (an $F$-space). A $B_0$-algebra is an $F$-algebra whose topology can be defined by a countable family of submultiplicative seminorms (equivalently, a complete metrizable locally convex algebra with continuous multiplication).

A two-sided ideal $I \subseteq A$ is called proper if $I \neq A$, and dense if its closure in $A$ equals $A$.

Question: Does there exist an $F$-algebra $A$ — or even a $B_0$-algebra — such that every proper (two-sided) ideal of $A$ is dense in $A$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up related work on dense ideals in F-algebras and B0-algebras (e.g., results connecting dense principal ideals to discontinuity of inversion and to topologically invertible elements), but no source clearly resolving the specific question of whether there exists an F-algebra (or B0-algebra) in which every proper ideal is dense. The status appears to remain unresolved in the literature accessible via search, so it is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on dense ideals including whether an F-algebra (or B0-algebra) can have all proper ideals dense.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in the survey on dense ideals in topological algebras.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open problems regarding ideal theory for F-algebras, including dense principal ideals and topologically invertible elements.
status_evidence.claim: Related questions about dense ideals in F-algebras are noted to remain open.
